item.title: Nvidia hold first earnings call since former CEO's departure
item.description: Chip giant Nvidia held its first earnings call since the departure of former CEO Jensen Huang, as interim CEO Colette Kress takes over.

item.title: Columbia professor on whether Nvidia earnings call helped ease investors' concerns
item.description: Did Colette Kress, Nvidia's interim CEO, reassure shareholders in Tuesday's earning call? NPR's Leila Fadel asks Shiva Rajgopal of Columbia Business School.
item.content:encoded: Did Colette Kress, Nvidia's interim CEO, reassure shareholders in Tuesday's earning call? NPR's Leila Fadel asks Shiva Rajgopal of Columbia Business School.

item.title: Nvidia tries to get back to business
item.description: Nvidia quarterly earnings are in. But the biggest question isn't about past business performance it's about the company's future leadership.

item.title: Nvidia board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: The former Nvidia CEO said he would be "honored" to return if the board allowed. But the board says it has no intention of reinstating him.

item.title: Can Google win the AI race without killing its cash cow?
item.description: In late October, Google had the worst stock day in its history as a public company. The Planet Money newsletter asks: has Google been caught in "the innovator's dilemma"?

item.title: She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades
item.description: While the rise of AI continues to fuel the debate over whether college is worth the cost, apprenticeships in the skilled trades are having a moment, drawing in people of all backgrounds including college graduates.

item.title: New rule aims to close loophole on chip exports
item.description: The Commerce Department released a new rule designed to make it harder for China to gain access to America's most powerful computer chips using third-country data centers.

item.title: Commerce Department under pressure for delaying export controls on Nvidia chips
item.description: The U.S. Commerce Department is under scrutiny for clearing Chinese companies to handle Nvidia chips, despite national security concerns from cabinet officials and U.S. intelligence agencies.

item.title: These economists say in-person work boosts creativity, but office mandates fall short
item.description: A pair economists argue in a new book that people are more creative and productive when they work together in person. But it's not enough for employers to simply order workers back to the office.

item.title: Is there an opening for Nvidia's competitors, now that Jensen Huang is out?
item.description: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with Dylan Patel of the AI and semiconductor research firm SemiAnalysis about Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, and whether it opens up the field for Nvidia's competitors.
